title: Whole f80r.14 as an image-location statement with coupled mirror predicates
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. A full twelve-group hypothesis says that an image in a plane mirror is directly opposite the object, behind the mirror, at equal perpendicular distance. The written remainder supplies three simultaneous claims about one pair, distinguishing plane reflection from a same-size half-turn. This gives IDEA351 a concrete target sentence and explicit lexical/syntactic debts; it does not claim an optical image owner.

finite_content_grammar.reference_rule: One image, one mirror and one original object are shared by all three predicates. The source-object role is resolved by the final written OBJECT. The mirror named in the first noun phrase remains the reference for behind and distance. No predicate can silently choose a different mirror or object.
finite_content_grammar.scope_rule: The copula governs three coordinated predicates; juxtaposition is the explicitly hypothesized coordination construction. It does not assert a time sequence or physical motion. The image is an apparent location, not a second material body manufactured behind a surface.
finite_content_grammar.writing_limit: This is one complete provisional sentence grammar with relational arguments, not a fixed-length source projection or cipher. A finite common realization for other complete sentences and the internal word parts remains unknown. No new per-occurrence glossary, optional erased word or source-count match is allowed.

coupled_assertions_in_the_written_remain.claim: Image and object have the same perpendicular foot on the same mirror.
The image lies on the opposite side of that mirror from the object.
Their absolute perpendicular distances from that mirror are equal.

exact_semantic_consequence.setup: Let the mirror cross-section be line M with unit normal n and equation n dot x = c. Let O be the nondegenerate original point and I its proposed image point.
exact_semantic_consequence.normal_alignment: The tangential projection of I equals the tangential projection of O.
exact_semantic_consequence.distance: abs(n dot I-c) = abs(n dot O-c).
exact_semantic_consequence.combined: All three require I = O - 2*(n dot O-c)*n. A separate free image location for each predicate is forbidden.
exact_semantic_consequence.nondegeneracy: O is not on the mirror. For an extended object, each corresponding point must use the same mirror; point names may be jointly renamed but not rematched independently.

concrete_rival_and_generated_example.status: Modern illustrative coordinates, not manuscript measurements, pixels or a historical transcription.
concrete_rival_and_generated_example.same_consequences: Reflection and half-turn both put the point behind the line at perpendicular distance 3; rigid size preservation also does not distinguish them.
concrete_rival_and_generated_example.different_written_consequence: Only reflection preserves the perpendicular foot (2,0). The half-turn has foot (-2,0), so the qotchy alignment claim would fail while the rest of the distance/side predicates still hold.
concrete_rival_and_generated_example.weaker_rival: If qotchy merely meant appears rather than directly opposite, the same written side/distance remainder would leave tangential image position free. The restrictive optical predicate is therefore a substantive lexical assumption, not an observed fact.
concrete_rival_and_generated_example.symmetries: Global rigid coordinate changes and scale remain gauges. A point on the turning axis can make the half-turn rival indistinguishable. A single freely placed mirror/object/image triple can always be fitted and earns no semantic credit.
